transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29 10:30 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orion CTO), Tom Baxter (Orion SRE), Jordan Lee (Orion ML), Sasha (Orion PM)

Summary/Notes (auto): reserve buffer sizing, eviction policy for KV/prefix cache, simulation results, pricing options, next steps.

[00:00] Alex Chen: alright everyone good morning, thanks for jumping on, uh today's the weekly sync on the POC — focus is reserve buffer and eviction behavior during bursts.
[00:18] Priya Nair: morning, thanks. quick ask up front, we want two options from you — a conservative reserve and a lower-cost plan we can propose to finance.
[00:27] Maya Singh: yep we prepared three sim profiles, two that Diego ran last night — i'll share the sheet after — they mirror your production traces you sent, compressed a bit.
[00:38] Tom Baxter: just to be clear, our production peaks hit ~600 tps for short bursts but spike to 1.2k for like 40-90s on heavy nightly jobs, so the tail is important.
[00:52] Diego Ramos: yeah we tried to capture that — profile A steady 200, B 500 with 30s spikes, C 1200 for 60s. we instrumented token-level latency and token cost.
[01:10] Jordan Lee: one ask — please show 99th perc latencies not just median, we care about user-facing latency.
[01:18] Maya Singh: absolutely, we included p50/p95/p99 in the spreadsheet. p99 is where the eviction/fallback shows up.
[01:27] Alex Chen: quick primer: reserve buffer is essentially reserved Dedicated capacity sitting idle to absorb sudden bursts; eviction policy governs which requests or model variants are demoted when buffer saturates — fallback routes to smaller quantized variant or a hosted-tier with slightly higher latency but lower cost.
[01:50] Priya Nair: curious about data residency — if a fallback goes to hosted variant, does data ever leave our VPC?
[01:58] Maya Singh: good q; in your Private/Dedicated vibration we can pin all traffic, but fallback to hosted will only be allowed if you opt in — otherwise our policy is to degrade gracefully within Dedicated (evict low-priority models or non-critical routes).
[02:15] Tom Baxter: ok that's important, Priya is firm on no cross-tenant hosted fallback for PHI.
[02:23] Alex Chen: noted. we'll remove hosted fallback from the canary config unless you explicitly allow it.
[02:29] Sasha: small note — finance will want delta cost between 25% buffer and 50% buffer.
[02:34] Alex Chen: yes we'll show both.
[02:38] [03:00] Maya Singh: jumping into the sim results: for profile B (500 tps with 30s spikes) a 25% reserve absorbed 78% of spikes with p99 latency ~220ms; with 50% reserve absorbed 94% and p99 ~160ms. but cost delta is roughly +37% for the 50% buffer versus 25% on the committed monthly.
[03:28] Tom Baxter: 220ms p99 is acceptable for us for most flows, the main concern is the 1.2k overnight spikes — how did profile C behave?
[03:38] Diego Ramos: profile C exhausted buffer in about 18s with 25% reserve, triggered eviction policy. eviction removed cached prefixes for background batch reranking flows first — that freed up ~18% capacity, then we started demoting large-context chat model variants to 8-bit quantized versions which added ~120ms CPU decode overhead. net p99 hit 480ms during sustained 60s spike.
[04:10] Jordan Lee: 480ms is borderline but could be fine for async batch jobs; for interactive chat we need <350ms ideally.
[04:20] Maya Singh: recommendation: for interactive chat routes keep 50% reserve for initial canary; for background/async routes test a 25% buffer with aggressive eviction on low-priority flows.
[04:35] Priya Nair: can you explain the eviction order? what gets evicted first?
[04:41] Diego Ramos: yes, eviction policy is tiered: 1) prefix/KV cache entries for low-importance routes; 2) non-critical batch rerank caches; 3) demote model variants (quantization); 4) as last resort queue or reject non-authenticated dev traffic.
[04:59] Tom Baxter: what about token caching correctness — will eviction cause higher upstream token regen cost?
[05:07] Maya Singh: some increased token cost yes, because prefix cache evictions cause re-priming tokens. we measured a +6-12% token count increase in the clean-up window.
[05:18] Jordan Lee: any risk of cache thrash if bursts come in waves?
[05:23] Diego Ramos: good catch — we simulate wave patterns too: if bursts recur within cache TTL we saw thrash unless we set a cooldown on eviction for the same keys — we recommended a 120s cooldown to stabilize.
[05:37] Alex Chen: also note that the runtime uses per-route KV isolation, so we can tune eviction priority at route granularity which gives you control to protect critical chat flows.
[05:48] [06:00] Priya Nair: security — KMS and audit logs: if we demote to quantized variant does that change encryption keys or logs?
[06:10] Maya Singh: no, model quantization is an execution-time change, audit logs still record model version and quantization flag and all requests remain under your KMS key. no key escrow or cross-tenant data movement.
[06:25] Sasha: finance question again — is it simpler to buy higher commit and reduce buffer or keep lower commit and pay burst overage? which is cheaper?
[06:35] Alex Chen: depends on burst frequency. our calc: if bursts are frequent (weekly peaks) commit+buffer beats overage; if rare one-offs, overage is cheaper. we'll include a simple TCO table in the pricing email.
[06:52] Tom Baxter: can we try a hybrid: 25% reserve but with auto-burst credit for occasional 2-3 minute surges?
[07:00] Diego Ramos: yes we can configure burst credits — it's essentially a short-lived soft capacity baked into your plan — we simulated a 3-minute credit and it absorbed two of three 60s spikes in our trace while keeping costs closer to the 25% buffer option.
[07:18] Jordan Lee: will that affect autoscaling SLOs? how quickly do instances spin up?
[07:24] Maya Singh: autoscaler ramps in two phases: hot-pool instant routing + scale-up slower provisioning. reserve buffer and burst credits give you immediate headroom; long sustained increases still trigger normal scale-up.
[07:36] Priya Nair: for canary we need documented rollback steps if the evictions cause user regressions.
[07:44] Alex Chen: we'll provide a rollback playbook: flip eviction policy to conservative, disable host- fallback, and route critical traffic to pinned nodes.
[07:54] [08:00] Sasha: can you share the spreadsheet now?
[08:03] Maya Singh: i posted a link in the chat — it's the sim_results_v2 sheet. note some columns are auto-calculated and the p99 column has interpolation artifacts — apologies if numbers look a bit off, transcription note: spreadsheets sometimes auto-round.
[08:24] Tom Baxter: i see the sheet — where's the token-cost delta?
[08:29] Diego Ramos: token-cost column is near the right, but the big driver was increased prefix re-priming when eviction occurred.
[08:36] Jordan Lee: did you test with our RAG index size? the index keys are large and prefix cache hit-rate differs.
[08:43] Maya Singh: yes we used a trimmed version of your RAG index — we recommend increasing per-route cache size for RAG read paths or instrument more fine-grained cache keys.
[08:54] Priya Nair: Ops will insist on no hosted fallback and strict SSO audit, are we good there?
[08:59] Alex Chen: yes, we'll remove hosted fallback for this customer by default; SSO/SAML and audit logs are available in Dedicated/Private.
[09:08] Sasha: last thing — can you give us a simple recommended config for the canary? just a one-pager.
[09:12] Maya Singh: recommended canary: 50% reserve for interactive chat routes; 25% reserve for background routes + 3-minute burst credit; eviction cooldown 120s; eviction order as discussed; no hosted fallback; metrics to watch: p99 latency, failed calls, token-cost delta, eviction rate.
[09:33] Priya Nair: sounds good. timeline?
[09:36] Alex Chen: we'll send pricing and the one-pager by Monday (2026-11-02). Maya will share sims by Thursday (2026-11-05). then we schedule the canary week of 2026-11-09.
[09:48] Tom Baxter: i'll confirm the canary window internally and share the 7-day histograms.
[09:53] Jordan Lee: quick note about regression testing — we'll run a small synthetic workload against canary endpoints to validate p99 before routing live traffic.
[09:59] Alex Chen: perfect. any other blockers?
[10:02] Priya Nair: none from me. thanks team.
[10:06] Alex Chen: thanks everyone — recap and action items in the email follow-up.
[10:10] [END]
